contributions.statement: When an agent proposes a harness or prompt change, require a written prediction of which failure class it fixes and what it must not regress, grade it against the eval result, and keep the graded predictions in a committed belief log.
contributions.evidence: §4.2 Table 1: BCO beats a matched loop lacking only the world model on all five benchmarks held-out (e.g., GAIA 0.343 -> 0.495, TB2.0 0.470 -> 0.492). One trajectory per method; Table 3 run-to-run range 0.11-0.13 exceeds the small TB2.0/AppWorld gaps; content ablation p=0.125.

contributions.statement: Bound any persistent scratchpad that is re-injected every turn; an unbounded belief document overflowed context on a more verbose model and left 65-99 of 372 tasks with no output, while a 16-exchange sliding window completed all.
contributions.evidence: §4.3 Fig. 3, App. D Table 6: AppWorld after target-model swap, BCO 0.516-0.532 vs vanilla 0.538-0.685; 99/77/65 no-output tasks at high/medium/low effort.

reason: The prediction-then-grade discipline is a concrete, host-neutral addition to harness tuning with consistent-direction evidence; the unbounded-scratchpad failure is a real but single-observation warning.
